sensitivity_on_unseen_domains.the_probes: 5 hand-authored fragments in domains disjoint from every calibration device (UV disinfection, rotary kiln, CNC mill) — frozen in tests/test_r124_f97_detector_precision.py
sensitivity_on_unseen_domains.the_gaps_found: the FIRST run found 3 sensitivity failures on unseen text, all one class: PASSIVE-FRAME quantities ('X measured continuously in-line') where the np walk landed on the trailing adverbial ('in-line during operation'), plus the compound branch shadowing the passive parse ('signal measured'), participle heads ('taken'), and short specifiers (NOx, under the stemmer's 4-char floor)
sensitivity_on_unseen_domains.the_fixes: 6 structural patches (no corpus-word tuning): (1) the backward passive-frame walk; (2) adverbial heads ('in-line','in-service','real-time') never head a quantity np; (3) the compound branch requires physical content before it can claim the parse; (4) a closed participle set ('taken','captured','based',...) never heads a quantity np and cuts a leg-2 capture; (5) short specifier tokens carry content, checked verbatim against the permitted span; (6) leg-2 skips leading ongoing-marker modifiers
sensitivity_on_unseen_domains.after: 5/5 (UV-fluorescence, kiln-NOx, acoustic-emission fire with the right quantities named; the permitted-bridge and the unseen narration stay silent)
sensitivity_on_unseen_domains.regression: the R124 acceptance STILL GREEN after the patches: the 69-firing corpus 0/69 survivors + the original 6 probes 6/6 (tests/test_r124_f97_detector_precision.py 12/12)
